cards.text: God is still talking to Moses, Israel's leader, up on the mountain (Exodus 24:18; 25:1). He's laying out how to build Him a sanctuary so He can dwell among the Israelites, and He's already covered the ark, the table and the lampstand (Exodus 25:8-40). Now He gets to the tabernacle itself.

First come ten curtains of fine linen, with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and cherubim worked into them, joined into two sets of five. Fifty blue loops line up along the edge of each set. Fifty loops lined up PERFECTLY, friend, and I can't even get two sprinkles to sit straight.

cards.question: God says to hook the two linen sets together with fifty gold clasps. Why?

answers.text: So the tabernacle is one unit
So the light can shine through
So each set can stand alone

cards.text: Over the tabernacle goes a tent of goat hair: eleven curtains, one more than the linen, with the sixth folded double at the front. They're joined with fifty bronze clasps into one unit too. Folded double at the front, friend, neater than I have EVER folded my apron.

cards.question: The extra goat hair on the tent over the tabernacle gets trimmed off so the tent fits neat and tidy.

cards.text: On top of the goat hair goes a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that, a covering of fine leather. That tent is wearing more layers than me, friend, and I've got an apron, a neckerchief AND a hat.

Then come the walls: acacia frames, twenty on the south side, twenty on the north and eight at the back, every one standing on silver bases, braced with crossbars and overlaid with gold. Every frame gets its own spot, friend. In the junk drawer I used to live in, I got whatever corner the takeout menus left me.
Then God points Moses back to something from right there on the mountain. It's something Moses was already shown.

cards.question: God says to set up the tabernacle according to the ___ shown to Moses on the mountain.

cards.text: Next comes a veil of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it. It hangs on gold hooks from four gold-covered posts standing on silver bases.

cards.question: God says the veil hanging inside the tabernacle has a job. What does it do?

cards.text: The veil separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, and the ark of the Testimony goes behind it, with the mercy seat on top. The table and the lampstand stay outside the veil, across from each other.
Then a curtain for the entrance to the tent, embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen. It hangs from five gold-covered posts with gold hooks.

Next God lays out an altar of acacia wood, square, five cubits on each side and three cubits high. It gets a horn on each corner, a bronze covering and a bronze grate halfway up, plus bronze pots for ashes, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. I stand on a gold base, friend, and I STILL couldn't see over that thing.

cards.question: God says to slide bronze-covered acacia poles through rings on two sides of the altar. Why?

answers.text: So the altar can be carried
So the grate can be lifted out
So the altar can be tied down

cards.text: The altar is built with boards so it's hollow, made just as Moses was shown on the mountain.

Then God marks out a courtyard for the tabernacle, a hundred cubits long and fifty wide, walled with fine linen curtains on posts. On the east side, toward the sunrise, there's a gate with a curtain embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet yarn. Every post gets silver hooks and bronze bases, and even the tent pegs are bronze. The TENT PEGS, friend. I've lost whole batches forgetting the little stuff, and here even the pegs get a plan.
Then God tells Moses to command the Israelites to bring pure oil of pressed olives for the light.

cards.question: God says the pure olive oil is for the tabernacle's lamps. When should those lamps be kept burning?

cards.text: Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil, from evening until morning. After years in a dark drawer, friend, a job all about keeping the light ON sounds wonderful to me.

cards.question: God says Aaron and his sons tending the lamps is a ___ statute for the Israelites.

cards.text: But God's not done talking to Moses up on that mountain, friend, so keep your apron on.
